cells.tense: You're deciding and moving, here, with your own hand on it — no rehearsal, no waiting for the room to agree.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you'd normally carry to the finish alone, and before you start, say out loud to one person what you noticed — that opens a second set of eyes where you usually keep only your own.
cells.core:
You know how far you can go before you break, and you act from that number instead of testing it. Something needs a call and you make it, then you carry what follows without asking anyone to make it lighter. People around you can feel the floor under them because you're standing on it.

Try one thing today that isn't carrying: before you move on something, say what you saw to whoever's nearby — one sentence, no case to make. Then let the reply land before you act. You'll still decide. You'll just be deciding with something in the room you didn't have to make yourself.
cells.sheetLine: You decide and you carry it — and you don't wait for permission to start.
cells.verb: deciding and moving first, on your own say-so
cells.place: the part of you that bears weight and stays standing under it

cells.tense: You're already braced against a break that hasn't happened, loading up for a stretch nobody's asked you to walk yet.
cells.ask: Open a notebook and write, in one sentence, the pattern you're braced against — then close it and leave it shut for the day; what that gives you is a trained eye on the structure itself, not on the next wall.
cells.core:
When it's going well, the structure you hold is one you chose. You look at what's coming, name the shape of it, and take on only the parts that earn the weight. Things stay reliable around you because you know what you're holding and why.

Right now you're ahead of it. Every load is already on your back before it arrives, and bracing is eating what the load needs. Step back once and look at one thing you're holding up. Write down what you think is coming, in one line, then close the notebook and leave it. Seeing the pattern clearly is the move — not preparing for it harder.
cells.sheetLine: You're bracing for the next break, and the bracing is costing you the load.
cells.verb: deciding and moving first, on your own say-so
cells.place: the part of you that bears weight and stays standing under it

cells.tense: You watched a moment pass and decided not to go first like that again — and you're still at the place that decision got made.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you've been putting off deciding and do one move on it today — make the call, put your name on a page, set the date — what you get back is momentum your body can stand on instead of a plan you keep holding.
cells.core:
When you're holding and it's going well, you know what to keep and what to set down. You decide without asking anyone to make the decision smaller, and your body trusts the call after it's made. There's a steadiness in you the people around you can lean on without asking.

Where you are now, the moment is behind you and you're still at it. Nothing's drawing power forward, so the deciding has gone quiet. Don't push harder into what's empty — do one small thing with a finish you can see. A call. A line signed. A date on a page. A body starts moving again from a finished act, not from a promise.
cells.sheetLine: You keep the option open and call it holding — the decision is what's actually stalled.
cells.verb: deciding and moving first, on your own say-so
cells.place: the part of you that bears weight and stays standing under it

cells.tense: You're already the one holding the line, and the way you tell it, the line is just there.
cells.ask: Name one thing you're carrying and say plainly that you're the one carrying it — to yourself or one person — and what you get is weight that's yours instead of weight that's merely present.
cells.core:
When you're bearing something, you can usually say which part of the load is yours and which belongs to the situation. Naming it is what lets the weight rest by knowing what it is, and the people around you get a center they can lean on.

Right now you're sitting there, the deciding is running fine, and the one doing it hasn't been named. You fix the thing, you make the plan, you hold the line — but if anyone asked, the sentence starts with the situation, not with you. This isn't more effort. It's saying true about where the weight actually lives.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding the line either way — naming it is what makes it yours.
cells.verb: deciding and moving first, on your own say-so
cells.place: the part of you that bears weight and stays standing under it

The record says the capacity is endurance and holding; it does not say the person holds in their body specifically, and a reader could reasonably say their version is that they go quiet and agree with everyone while their hands do the deciding.
